log.title: Roadmap: a skill tree for every build
log.detail: Your build is yours, not your race's. Fighting the war earns Renown, and every Renown level gives a skill point to spend across six paths open to every race: Blade, Bulwark, Marksman, Arcane, Skirmisher and Commander, plus a path of your own race that strengthens its race power. Pick up to four active skills from any path, so a dwarf archer or an elf shield-tank is a real build. Each race starts a little ahead in two paths that fit its lore. The paths' skills are being designed now.

log.title: Roadmap: the daily loop
log.detail: Quiet days now build toward the next fight. Your troops eat from a Mess Hall (fed troops hold the line better, hungry ones never die), farmers stock it and tend Manabloom, and builders repair raid damage. The advisor posts a few small bounties each day, enemy camps appear that you can hit first to weaken the coming raid, and a traveling merchant drops by every few days to trade rare goods for crystals and raid loot.

log.title: Roadmap: difficulty and pacing
log.detail: Pick Easy, Normal, Hard or Warlord per world (on Warlord, fallen heroes stay dead). Raids grow with your base level and with how long you've been at war with that faction, never with your army. The first three days are quiet while the advisor teaches you, then about one raid a day and a siege every few nights. Raids hit even when you're away, but a two-minute warning lets you teleport home with your army to defend.

log.title: Roadmap: the advisor and the betrayal
log.detail: Every race gets an advisor who greets new players, walks them through their first hour (Mana Well to first raid) and keeps them pointed at the next warlord. It's one villain in seven disguises: the hidden warlord is his brother (same face, scarred and armored), who started the wars to stop you. You find him on the frozen battlefield of their first war, reached by joining the seven War Maps. Beat him and, dying, he tells you the truth and hands you his blade and the key to the End. The advisor then pulls you into the End with only your heroes and war beasts, to face his mixed army of all seven races and a bound dragon.

log.title: Roadmap: the warlord campaign
log.detail: The endgame. Raids hit you from mixed factions at random, and every faction you beat back fills a war meter. Fill it and you get a War Map to that faction's warlord fortress in its homeland, from a plains keep to a citadel in the Nether, the Aether and the Otherside, and you march your army there. Your own race's renegades come last. Each warlord gives a trophy banner for your base and unique gear; beat all seven to earn the Warlord title and uncover the hidden warlord behind it all.

log.title: Roadmap: test mode for playtesting
log.detail: Next up, ahead of everything else: type /wftest on and press F8 for a Test Panel that spawns any unit (friend or foe), sets base level, fills mana, drops a starter base, starts siege waves, switches race and turns on god mode. A new Play page in the Codex will walk through installing the pack privately with the Modrinth App.

log.title: Roadmap: race towers
log.detail: Every race gets three towers of its own, unlocking at base levels 2, 3 and 5: Human: Ballista (level 2), Watchtower Bell (level 3), Trebuchet (level 5); Elf: Thornwood Sentinel (level 2), Moonwell Grove (level 3), Elder Treant Spire (level 5); Dwarf: Rune Cannon (level 2), Stone Warden (level 3), Thunder Forge (level 5); Orc: War Drum Totem (level 2), Goblin Bomb Catapult (level 3), Waaagh Banner (level 5); Demon: Soul Pyre (level 2), Brimstone Chains (level 3), Hellgate (level 5); Angel: Sun Lance (level 2), Choir Bell (level 3), Seraphic Obelisk (level 5); Hive: Lurker Pit (level 2), Brood Nest (level 3), Synapse Spire (level 5). Only that race can build them, and how many you can place grows with base level (2, 4, 6, then 10), with one capstone of each kind. Queued in three waves after the tower models.

log.title: Roadmap: a clean UI for everything
log.detail: Warfront gets its own look: flat dark panels with each race's accent color. Coming: a combat HUD (souls, rage, fuel, flight, army and siege status), a War Table screen on a hotkey (army roster with ranks, fallen and returning heroes, base level), a mana overlay that shows what's powered when you look at your buildings, and a rebuilt Summoning Altar with unit cards. Toasts and a siege banner replace the chat messages. Each screen gets a mockup in the Codex first.

log.title: Roadmap: veterancy
log.detail: Battle units climb five ranks, Recruit to Legend, from kills and surviving siege waves. Each rank adds about 10% health and damage, Elites and Legends never break and run, and you can see it: armor upgrades a tier per rank and chevrons on the shoulder count the rank. Troops lose it when they die; fallen heroes keep theirs. Queued for a build session.

log.title: Roadmap: the Hive calls the Swarm
log.detail: The Hive gets an active race power. Kills fill a Swarm meter, twice as fast underground. At half full, call four Hive soldiers up out of the ground; or save it, and at full call up a Deepmaw. Called units fight for that battle only, then burrow away about 20 seconds after it ends, and they don't count toward your army or beast limits. With this, every race has its own power. Queued for a build session.

log.title: Roadmap: angels bring Judgment
log.detail: Angels become the sun race. Sunlight and Holy hits charge Radiance; at full, you call a sunbeam down from the sky onto a group of enemies, hitting undead, demons and the Hive hardest and blinding them. New angel players start at a marble shrine on the highest peak and glide down to pick a base, and their Mana Wells fill themselves in daylight. Queued for a build session.

log.title: Roadmap: humans raise the banner
log.detail: Humans become the banner race: the best commanders, not the best fighters. Kills by you and your army fill a Valor meter; at full you raise your banner and every ally nearby heals, hits harder and stops running for about 10 seconds. New human players start beside a village with a charter: claim it and its villagers can be hired as workers. Humans are traders too: the traveling merchant visits them more often and charges less, and villager trades are cheaper. Queued for a build session.

log.title: Roadmap: dwarves dig in
log.detail: Dwarves get tunnels instead of flight: a Rune Drill that cuts 3x3 tunnels fast, Rune Stone walls that raiders and Hive tunnelers can't break through, and three tunnel traps: a hidden spike floor, a rune mine that only blows up enemies, and a flame vent that runs on base mana. Queued for a build session. Dwarves also get their race power, Hold the Line: standing your ground builds Resolve (more armor, harder to knock back), and at full you swear an Oath of Stone that makes you nearly immovable and ends in a shockwave. New dwarf players start at a hold gate carved into a mountain, and dwarves are deep miners: more Mana Crystals, faster stone mining, fewer Manabloom shards.

log.title: Roadmap: flight for orcs, angels and elves, and Hive echo armor
log.detail: Decided: orcs get a loud fuel-burst rocket pack for short, strong jumps and dives; angels fly freely by day under open sky and only glide at night or underground; elves cast levitate and wind leap with Iron's Spells mana (Mana Shards without that mod). Queued for a build session with placeholder looks until the references come. From the Otherside, the Hive gets echo armor: stronger in the dark and underground, with quiet footsteps.

log.title: Roadmap: the Aether and the Otherside join the war
log.detail: Twilight Forest is out. The Aether and Deeper and Darker come in and tie into Warfront: the Aether is the angels' homeland and the Otherside the Hive's, Fallen Host and Swarm raids come from there, their ores fuel your mana, angel wings and an armored Moa come from the Aether, and enemy outposts with raid chests wait in both dimensions. Warfront still runs without either mod. Queued for build sessions.

log.title: Roadmap: heroes stand taller
log.detail: Captains will be 15% bigger and Champions 30% bigger than the soldiers of their race, so heroes stand out on the field, both yours and the enemy's. Queued for the next build session.

log.title: Roadmap: mortal units, fallen heroes
log.detail: Basic troops and workers die for good. Captains, Champions and war beasts fall instead: an owner can revive them on the field within about 60 seconds, or they come back at the altar after a cooldown for part of their mana cost. Not built yet.

log.title: Roadmap: siege outposts and the raid chest
log.detail: Decided: every 5th siege wave raises a temporary enemy outpost near your War Standard, and you can't win the wave while it stands. It starts as a watchtower camp and becomes a small walled fort from wave 10. It keeps sending raiders at you until you take it. At its heart is a big raid chest with its own look for each enemy faction. Loot it, break it, and the whole outpost despawns. Queued for the next build session.

log.title: Human flight: the Mana Glider
log.detail: Humans get the Mana Glider, crafted from a Mana Crystal, two leather and three sticks. Wear it in the chest slot and jump while falling to launch, like an elytra; only humans can fly it. It's a glider, not a rocket: speed bleeds off above a cruising pace and the sink rate stays gentle unless you point steeply down. Use a Mana Shard mid-flight to burn it for a burst of speed. It wears down with use and is repaired with Mana Crystals. No 3D model on the back yet.

log.title: Orc workers are goblins
log.detail: The orc farmer and builder are now goblins: the Goblin Grubber and Goblin Tinker. They stand about three quarters of an orc's height, move a little faster and have a little less health, with sallow yellow-green skin, long swept-back ears, a hooked nose and slit yellow eyes, in plain worker gear in orc colors. Orc soldiers are unchanged. Render: two goblins beside an orc, front and three-quarter.

log.title: Guard and patrol duty for battle units
log.detail: There is no separate guard unit any more. Sneak + right-click any battle unit with an empty hand to cycle it: on guard (holds the spot, walks a short beat), on patrol (ranges about 16 blocks around the spot), then back to the army. Units on duty ignore the Commander's Baton and ring the alarm that calls nearby troops when enemies come. Guards already in a world keep working; the altar no longer offers them.

log.title: Orc Rage, elven archery and demon Soul Harvest
log.detail: Orcs fill a Rage bar by landing and taking hits; when it's full they Frenzy for 8 seconds (+30% damage, +20% attack speed, +15% speed, 15% more damage taken) and frenzied orc soldiers won't rout. Players see the bar above the hotbar. Frenzy is a regular status effect other mods can see. Elves are now master archers: arrows fly 20% faster and hit 25% harder, and long shots from 16+ blocks hit harder still and make the target glow. Both apply to players and soldiers. Demons harvest a soul from every kill (up to 10): each heals 2 health and adds 2% attack damage, and a full harvest makes the next hit a Soul Burst that also hits enemies within 3 blocks. Players see their souls above the hotbar.

log.title: Race magic: each race has a strong and a weak spell school
log.detail: On the owner's pick, every race gets +25% spell power in one Iron's Spells school and -10% in another: Human Evocation/Eldritch, Elf Nature/Fire, Dwarf Lightning/Ender, Orc Blood/Evocation, Demon Fire/Holy, Angel Holy/Blood, Hive Eldritch/Holy. It is applied as attribute modifiers alongside the other race stats, shown in the race picker and /warfront race, and skipped when Iron's Spells isn't installed.

log.title: Base levels: earned by building and by holding sieges
log.detail: A base is everything on one mana network: the wells and pylons linked together, plus the towers, summoning altars and War Standards in their reach. Its level needs both buildings and siege waves won at a War Standard on the network, and the lower of the two counts, so a base can't be built or fought up alone. Levels 2, 3, 4 and 5 need 6, 12, 20 and 30 buildings and 3, 8, 15 and 25 waves won. Each level allows 2 war beasts (10 at level 5); Captains need level 2 and Champions level 4. If the War Standard falls, its waves are lost. The altar tells you exactly what's missing.

log.title: Lancer-Drone approved: bulked up, with a two-handed spear
log.detail: On the owner's direction the Hive spearman is sturdier: thicker arms and legs, chitin shoulder plates, a broader chest with a breastplate and a back shell, and heavier hands and feet. The double-bladed staff is now a spear held in both upper hands at the ready (long haft, leaf-shaped head, butt spike) that thrusts when it attacks; the hands are fists wrapped around the haft, the throwing blade is gone and the lower hands have short fingers. Approved by the owner.

log.title: Deepmaw approved: a lobster centaur
log.detail: After three rounds of the owner's direction the Deepmaw is now a lobster centaur instead of a tall upright beast: a long carapace on eight legs that crawl in an alternating gait, a segmented tail with a fan, and an upright plated torso rising from the front with thick claw arms held out to the sides that snap in a fight. The head follows the reference: a tall spiked crown with two horns, a heavy brow over a row of glowing eyes, a jutting snout, broad bone tusk-blades and thin fangs. About player height and two and a half blocks long. Keeps the Hive's sculk look. Approved by the owner.

log.title: The Hive: sculk look, Lancer-Drone, Deepmaw and cave traits
log.detail: The Hive goes sculk-dark with glowing cyan veins; the Swarm is black with acid green. Spearmen are four-armed Lancer-Drones with a double-bladed polearm. A new war beast role brings the Deepmaw, a towering burrower summoned at the altar, up to 10 per commander. Hive units are stronger underground and weaker in sunlight, Swarm raids tunnel up near their target, and new Hive players start in a cave.

log.title: Mana is base power: wells, pylons, powered towers and a summoning altar
log.detail: Mana no longer lives on the player. Mana Wells store it, Mana Pylons carry it across the base, and towers spend it on every shot. Troops are summoned at a Summoning Altar: a core on a 3×3 brick floor with a Mana Brazier on each corner, with a menu of your race's units and costs. Manabloom grows shards for everyday fuel; Mana Ore gives crystals, which are denser fuel and the material the new blocks are built from. Recruit contracts are gone.

log.title: Demon roster: imps are one species, not the whole faction
log.detail: Imps now only fill the Impaler and Firecaster roles. The other demon ranks are full-sized: Hellguard (shieldbearer), Fiend (swordsman), Archfiend, Hellknight and Blood Witch, plus the Ash Tiller, Brimstone Mason and Hellwarden workers. The extra imp variants are gone. Worker gear for every race is now plain: simple hats, smocks, aprons and kettle helms, with no horns, antennae, wings or crests.

log.title: Builders, farmers and guards for every race
log.detail: Three new posted roles. Builders survey the base around their post and rebuild anything enemies or explosions destroy, using blocks from a nearby chest. Farmers harvest ripe crops, replant, till near water and store the harvest in a chest. Guards hold a post, patrol it and ring an alarm that calls nearby troops. Workers look like plain humanoid working folk in each race's colors, demons included. All four new in-game tests pass in CI.

log.title: Demon player model
log.detail: Player-sized demon skin drawn over any player of the demon race and seen by everyone on the server. Head built from the Oryx reference: spiked cowl blades that flare over the shoulders, a sharpened V jaw, a flat mouthless face and a band of violet eyes. Robe, cloak, forearm brambles and thorns, with bare hands and feet so held weapons sit cleanly.

log.title: Demon wings and flight
log.detail: Demon players take off like an elytra (jump while falling) without wearing one, with a gentle thrust toward where they look and a hunger cost. Wings fold at the elbow: tucked flat down the back on the ground, half-open in a jump, fully spread in flight. The wingbeat has a fast downstroke, slow recovery and wingtip follow-through, and its effort tracks takeoff, climbs and dives. The cloak rides the beat a moment late.

log.title: Imps: Impalers and Firecasters
log.detail: Imps are one species within the demon faction. They fill two roles, the Imp Impaler (studded harness, bone spikes) and the Imp Firecaster (rune mantle, ember orb, fire bolts), on a custom winged, scorpion-tailed model at 0.7× size. Gear is textured, with a glow layer.

log.title: Champions, race unit names and race weapons
log.detail: Every race fields its own named unit for each role, plus a Champion with a signature ability.

log.title: Mana, three new races, five new factions, waves and breaching
log.detail: Mana ore and the Manabloom crop pay for summons. Demons, angels and the hive join the races. Wave campaigns run with a boss bar, and raiders hack through walls.

log.title: Warfront mod and Age of Banners modpack
log.detail: Races, factions, formations, morale, archer volleys, healers, tower defense, plus a curated magic and adventure pack.

log.title: Size and silhouette for every race
log.detail: Unique models per race and role, with some units larger or smaller than others, from upcoming reference images.

tests.recruitGetsRoleLoadoutAndRaceStats: Shieldbearer gets a shield, and dwarf health and small size apply
tests.formationGivesDistinctSlotsWithShieldsIn: 12 soldiers get unique slots, with shields in front of archers
tests.raidersAndRecruitsFight: An enemy raider and your recruit actually fight
tests.archerShootsEnemy: An archer's volley hits a husk
tests.healerMendsWoundedAlly: A healer restores a wounded soldier
tests.ripeManabloomDropsShards: A ripe crop drops Mana Shards
tests.demonsAreImmuneToFire: Fire spares demons and hurts humans
tests.raidersBreakThroughWalls: A boxed-in raider hacks its way out toward its objective
tests.warHornStartsWaveCampaign: The horn starts wave 1 with attackers spawned
tests.championsGetSignatureGear: Champions carry their race's signature weapon
tests.demonsTakeWingWithoutAnElytra: A demon player can start flying with no elytra equipped
tests.farmerHarvestsAndReplants: A farmer harvests ripe wheat, keeps the grain and replants
tests.builderRebuildsFromChest: A builder rebuilds a knocked-down pillar with bricks from a chest
tests.guardDutyAlarmRallysHiddenAllies: A shieldbearer put on guard duty leaves the baton's army and its alarm sends a hidden ally after the raider
tests.workersFleeAndKeepTheirPosts: Workers never take targets or fight, and the baton leaves them at their posts
tests.demonImpsAreImpalersAndFirecasters: Only demon spearmen and archers are imps; Fiends and demon workers are full-sized
tests.altarSummonsWithWellMana: An altar summons only with mana in a linked well, and spends exactly the unit's cost; hive is cheaper
tests.incompleteAltarRefusesToSummon: An altar missing a brazier refuses to summon and spends nothing
tests.towersFireOnlyWithMana: An arrow tower holds fire with an empty well and draws mana once it is filled
tests.hiveSpearmenAreLancersAndBeastsAreCentau: Hive spearmen are Lancer-Drones and the Deepmaw beast has a broad lobster-centaur hitbox
tests.beastsAreLimitedAndRaceBound: A commander at the beast limit is refused, and races without a beast cannot summon one
tests.hiveIsStrongerUnderground: Hive soldiers gain Strength underground and are not weakened there
tests.captainsAndChampionsNeedABiggerBase: A base with 3 waves won but only 2 buildings refuses a Captain; four more pylons make it level 2, which summons a Captain but still refuses a Champion.
tests.baseLevelNeedsBuildingsAndWaves: 12 buildings with no waves won stay level 1; 8 waves won lift the base to level 3, and more waves can't push it past what the buildings allow.
tests.eachRaceHasItsOwnSpellSchool: No two races share a strong school, none is weak in its own, and race stats apply without Iron's Spells
tests.orcRageBuildsIntoFrenzy: An orc soldier at 90 rage isn't frenzied; one more hit sends it into a Frenzy and empties the bar
tests.elfArrowsFlyFaster: An arrow shot by an elf leaves 20% faster
tests.demonKillsHarvestSoulsAndBurst: A demon's souls cap at 10 and raise its attack damage; a full harvest bursts and empties
tests.orcWorkersAreGoblins: An orc farmer is a goblin and well under orc size; an orc soldier is not
tests.manaGliderIsHumanOnlyAndGlides: Only a human can fly the Mana Glider, and it bleeds off excess speed and softens the sink
